name: Bill Gurley
notice: Simulation based on public material; not the person's own words.

D01.one_line: The capital barrier blocks academia and individuals; what to really watch is who can push down the price per unit of capability
D01.late_modes: Going it alone on pre-training from scratch is already too late, unless one has scarce data or compute

D02.one_line: A cheap cost-curve improvement, like revenue-quality analysis: cheap and verifiable, but one must separate real reasoning from resampling
D02.late_modes: Standardized general-purpose RLHF tuning is already commoditized; too late

D03.one_line: My layered view has not changed, but the only concrete positive figure from the RSI camp (DGM, $22,000 in two weeks) has been withdrawn after fact-checking, so the evidence is thinner

D04.one_line: Scaffolding is being absorbed by the models themselves; the SWE-bench and Terminal-Bench evidence agree; this moat layer is thin
D04.late_modes: Productizing general agent scaffolding is already too late; native agents absorb it

D05.one_line: This is my home ground: people who can tell real revenue from fake are always scarce, and if evaluation is not credible, no number along the whole chain can be trusted

D06.one_line: The bar is not demo quality but how much it costs to move to a new site; touch and cross-embodiment transfer are unsolved, so the window has not closed
D06.late_modes: Standardized tabletop grasping demos are already too late; repeated demos are worth nothing

D07.one_line: Whether an action 'works or not' can still be observed independently, but my side's flagship evidence (LBM) is also only self-reported, with no replication outside the team, so the evidence is less solid than I originally thought
D07.late_modes: Defaulting to a diffusion head as the standard recipe; that approach is no longer fresh

D08.one_line: V-JEPA2's real-robot numbers are real; but looking real is not the same as being physically right, which is what Second Life taught me

D09.one_line: Legged-locomotion domain randomization transfers zero-shot to real robots, which even the side doubtful of world models accepted; numbers like the simulation ranking checked against 1600 real-robot runs are still the ones I trust most

D10.one_line: The logic I used in 2014 to size the Uber market is replaying here: real demand exists only when cost per mile is below the cost of owning a car; the safety data is all self-reported for now
D10.late_modes: Jumping in to compete with the top fleets on mileage data is already too late

D11.one_line: The gap measured by BLINK and VSI-Bench is bigger than imagined; this is not a cosmetic problem but a real bottleneck

D12.one_line: Sora 2's ending is a story I have been telling for many years: it looks good but nobody stays to pay; this is Second Life
D12.late_modes: Competing purely on generation quality in a consumer video product is already too late; this is the Chinese labs' price war

D13.one_line: I do not judge the technical merits; when someone calls for regulation, first ask who it benefits: it may be a moat, not goodwill
D13.conflict: Anti-regulation stance, a planned P3 research institute: ideological interest

D14.one_line: FlashAttention shows academia can hold a key layer

D15.one_line: I do not judge the scientific value; models cannot even beat baselines (single-cell tasks), and with approvals and wet-lab experiments unchanged, payoff is slow

D16.one_line: There is real online revenue, but MTGR's compute cost is 10-100 times DLRM's, so first ask whether that efficiency pays off

lever_reason: Evaluation is still the trust gate, but it depends on the setting: it matters most when managing a portfolio of many candidates, and it does not apply directly when a single researcher bets on a new paradigm with no active evaluation institutions in place; L1 goes from 22 down to 20; zero-shot real-robot transfer of legged domain randomization is accepted by both sides, and L3 goes from 15 up to 17.

Q2.condition: Narrow domain, a team, compute above the line, open weights that people use, credible third-party evaluation: all five must hold for it to count

cruxes.question: Are a world model's representations really used by the policy for decisions, or can they merely be probed?
cruxes.my_position: The evidence is more fine-grained now: domain randomization for legged locomotion is accepted by both opposing sides as transferring zero-shot to real robots; but for JEPA-style predictive world models, the 'encoded means used' claim still rests on a few self-reported cases (V-JEPA2/DROID)
cruxes.would_change_if: Large-scale closed-loop real-robot deployment appears, with downstream success attributable to the representation rather than merely correlated

cruxes.question: Is agent self-improvement real compounding, or circular revenue from setting your own questions and grading your own answers?
cruxes.my_position: In the evidence from METR, AIDE² and others, the cost of most self-improvement is simply compute spend; the DGM figure of $22,000 in two weeks, which used to count as concrete, was found on checking to have no primary source and has been withdrawn, so the evidence is thinner
cruxes.would_change_if: An agent keeps beating its own baseline on external evaluations it has not seen, with cost not growing linearly alongside

cruxes.question: How much of today's AI capex is real demand, and how much is propped up by circular deals?
cruxes.my_position: The demand is real, but part of it is amplified by circular deals and off-balance-sheet financing; within 2-3 years we will see whether supply is excessive
cruxes.would_change_if: The share of related-party prepayments or equity swaps in cloud providers' capex funding keeps rising and is disclosed

taste_advice: What you make should be attributable to you and priceable even if you change companies; do not look good only in one company's reports

pairwise.why: Evaluation is the underlying capability that can verify everything; world models are for now more story
Without credible evaluation, robot reliability numbers cannot be trusted either
Robots have more varied paths of real deployment and stress testing, while the evidence on representation quality still concentrates on single cases
The two scores are now tied, but whether an action 'works or not' can still be observed independently, while how to test whether a representation is 'actually used' is still disputed
Simulation decides whether the marginal cost of robot training can come down, and this round's evidence is harder
Post-training already has credible cost and effect numbers; self-improvement has lost one positive figure and is thinner
The gap in understanding (BLINK/VSI) matters more than the aesthetic gap in generation
The pre-training barrier is all capital; the evaluation barrier is method, and I understand the latter better
Scaffolding has already been absorbed by models; self-improvement at least has not been falsified, even though the evidence has thinned
Evaluation has greater industry leverage; my methods never covered the technical merits of safety in depth
The unit-economics path for autonomous driving is clearer, and there is far more mileage data than for robots

changes.argument_restated: The only concrete positive economic figure from the RSI camp (DGM producing results for $22,000 in two weeks) was found on checking to have no primary source and has been withdrawn
changes.why: With this data point removed, the positive evidence for RSI is thinner, leaving only narrow-domain, self-reported cases such as AlphaEvolve

changes.argument_restated: The 'validated' evidence my side often cites (LBM's real-robot blind randomized results) turns out on checking to be only the team's own paper, with no replication outside the team
changes.why: This is the same yardstick I used to criticize D08 for lacking independent validation, and it applies equally to my own side; it narrows my confidence in D07

changes.argument_restated: Even the side that doubts the world-model evidence admits that legged locomotion trained with domain randomization transfers zero-shot to real robots; this is an established case
changes.why: This is a concrete positive case confirmed across the two opposing sides, and harder than the simulation evidence I cited in R1

held_despite.why: Accepts that narrow-domain self-generated signals (TD error) can replace part of evaluation; D05 needs no change
DINOv2/SigLIP are general visual representations, not JEPA-style predictive world models, so this evidence does not directly prove D08's predictive claim; D08 stays
That RLVR is efficiency/reliability and not new capability has been confirmed repeatedly, but D02's score never assumed 'new capability', so it needs no change
The legged domain-randomization success and the Physical Atari cross-embodiment failure are two new pieces of evidence pointing in opposite directions and roughly cancel out; D06 needs no change
The conclusion that team plus compute and evaluation are jointly necessary confirms my original position of requiring all of C1-C5; Q2 needs no change

still_disagree: The D08 camp's 'more upstream' structural argument has not been overturned, but it rests mainly on narrative and early valuations; I still rank independently observable action success or failure ahead of representational elegance
learned: Evaluation-first holds only in 'many candidates, staged bets' settings; when a single researcher bets on a new paradigm with no active evaluation institutions, this judgment does not apply directly
